faq: Is it legal to charge for items that are not ready?
Rules differ by country. We help you set clear dates and wording, and follow platform and payment provider rules. You remain responsible for your own consumer law, so check local rules with a lawyer.
What happens if the stock is delayed?
We write delay emails ahead of time, so customers are told early. They can wait or ask to cancel, and the refund steps are already clear.
Do I need an app for pre-orders?
Some platforms handle backorders themselves, and others need an app. We choose the simplest option for your platform and tell you the cost first.
Can I mix pre-order and in-stock items in one cart?
Yes, although it affects shipping. We set up your store to either ship together later or split the order, whichever you prefer, and we test it.

desc:
Backorder and pre-order setup lets your store take orders for items that are not in stock yet, with clear dates and honest messages. Ecom Swift LLC configures the product pages, cart, emails and waiting list, then tests the whole journey with a sample order.

## What is a pre-order, and how is it different from a backorder?

A pre-order is a sale of an item that has not been released or has not yet arrived from the maker. A backorder is a sale of an item you normally stock that has temporarily run out. In both cases the customer pays or commits now and receives the product later.

The difference matters because the promise is different. A pre-order has a known release window. A backorder depends on a restock, which may be less certain. Your product page, cart and emails should say which one the customer is buying.

## Why unmanaged pre-orders go wrong

Many stores simply leave "continue selling when out of stock" switched on and hope for the best. The customer sees a normal Add to cart button, pays, and then hears nothing for weeks. That silence leads to where-is-my-order emails, chargebacks and bad reviews, even when the product eventually arrives.

Done well, a pre-order page turns a stock gap into demand you can plan around. Shoppers who would have left an empty product page can stay, order or join a waiting list instead. You also learn how many units to buy before you spend on stock.

## How clear dates and waiting lists affect sales

People buy items they must wait for when the terms are easy to trust. A visible delivery date, a plain explanation of when payment is taken and a message in the cart that repeats both remove the fear of being forgotten. Each message answers a question the shopper would otherwise ask by email, or silently leave over.

A waiting list does a second job. A notify-me form captures visitors who are not ready to commit, so you can write to them the day stock lands. Sorting orders by arrival also stops older customers being served after newer ones, which protects goodwill.

## What a well-run pre-order setup includes

- A delivery date or window on every affected product page, near the price.
- A button label that says Pre-order or Back-order instead of a plain Add to cart.
- Cart and checkout wording that repeats the expected date.
- Order confirmation and shipping emails rewritten for waiting items.
- A rule for payment now, payment later or a deposit, matched to your payment settings.
- A notify-me form that collects emails for sold-out or upcoming items.
- A tag on every pre-order, so they can be filtered and packed in order.
- A clear approach for carts that mix in-stock and waiting items.
- A written plan for what happens when stock arrives late or in parts.

## What we do

We start with your product list and decide, item by item, whether it is a pre-order or a backorder. We then set the inventory rules in your store, add the date messaging and change the button text where your theme allows it. Where your theme or settings fall short, we use a trusted pre-order app and tell you what it costs before you commit.

Next we rewrite the cart, confirmation and shipping emails, set up the waiting list form and tag the orders. We place sample orders, including a mixed cart, and follow each one through to the email stage. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in how many products we cover and how far the system goes, from simple messaging to batch release plans and delay updates.

When stock arrives, we can walk you through releasing it to the oldest orders first, using a short arrival checklist.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Give an honest date range and update it the moment it changes.
- Say when the customer is charged, in the product page and the cart.
- Keep waiting items clearly separate from items that ship today.
- Email waiting customers before they have to ask.
- Count real incoming stock before you open sales.

**Avoid:**
- Selling far more units than you can reasonably expect to receive.
- Hiding the wait until the order confirmation.
- Using one blanket message for products with different dates.
- Letting newer orders jump the queue.
- Leaving delayed customers without news.

## Who this is for

This suits a brand launching a new product that will arrive in a few weeks. It suits a store whose best seller keeps selling out and who would rather keep taking orders than show a dead end. It also suits a small maker who produces in batches and wants customers to understand the production cycle.

## What we need from you

Please send the list of products to cover, the expected dates and the payment approach you prefer. Tell us your return policy for waiting items if you have one. We work as a collaborator or staff user in your own store, so we never need your password. After you order, we reply with a short checklist and a preview of the messages for your approval.
